It can happen enough where it's not out of place. Typically if it is a word that English based, they will do something that sounds like it (ergo Computer is like Computeru Japanese never ends in a consonants). This is also typical for acronyms. We do the same with things like Poke'mon (Pocket Monsters).
Actually they mostly use longs in such cases, so a computer is actually "コンピューター". Or, closer to home, "アイドルマスター" and not "アイドルマステル".
All the other answers in this thread are right, too, but I would like to add that often in Japanese they often incorporate English words and phrases (and acronyms) just for the sake of sounding cool.
